THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE M G UMA  ORAL ORDER (PER: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE M G UMA) The petitioner being accused in Crime No.16/2025 of Women Police Station, Vijayapur pending on the file of the learned IV Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Vijayapura registered for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n), 417, 504 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 [for short, 'the IPC'] is seeking quashing the criminal proceedings.
2.

Heard Sri Sachin C. Angadi, learned counsel for the petitioner, and Sri Jamadar Shahabuddin,
learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 - State, NC: 2025:KHC-K:5120 HC-KAR Smt. Swati M.N., learned counsel for respondent No.2.
Perused the materials on record.

3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the criminal proceedings initiated against the petitioner is liable to be quashed invoking inherent power under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?"

My answer to the above point is in the 'Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 4. Respondent No.2 filed the first information with Women Police Station, Vijayapura against the accused alleging that, she was in love with accused.

Initially he induced her and they became close to Mallikarjun vs State Of Karnataka on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138177280/
2 one another and they were roaming around for sometime.
Taking advantage of this, the accused came to her house repeatedly and committed rape under the promise to NC: 2025:KHC-K:5120 HC-KAR marry her.
Later, he refused to marry her.
A panchayat in this regard was arranged in the police station, where the accused again promised to marry her.
Accordingly, the date of marriage was fixed on 23.02.2025.
All necessary arrangements were made by respondent No.2 and her family members.
But on 13.02.2025 the accused had called respondent No.2 and refused to marry her.
Therefore, the first information came to be filed requesting the police to register the case and to initiate legal action.
Accordingly, the police registered the case and undertook the investigation.
years.
The accused and respondent No.2 are majors and they have voluntarily had physical relationship.
It is not the contention of respondent No.2 that, even while having physical relationship with her, the accused had an intention to cheat her.
Simply because later he refused to marry her, the same cannot be a ground to invoke Sections 376 (2) (n) and 417 of the IPC.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:5120 HC-KAR 6.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has placed reliance on the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Jothiragawan vs. State Represented by the Inspector of Police and Another wherein similar set of facts were considered by the Hon'ble Apex Court and by placing reliance on its earlier decision in Prithvirajan vs. The State Represented by the Inspector of Police & Another2, the Apex Court reiterated the position of law that, the relationship between two major persons who are closely related, was consensual, breach of promise to marry does not automatically amount to rape, unless fraudulent intent existed at the time of taking the consent.

sentences.text: 7. The decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court is aptly applicable to the facts of the present case where respondent No.2 herself states that, they were close to each other and moving around together and accused had visited her house repeatedly which resulted in their physical relationship.

Subsequently, there arose some 2025 LiveLaw (SC) 347 Criminal Appeal No.282 of 2025 @
SLP(Crl.)No.12663 of 2022 NC: 2025:KHC-K:5120 HC-KAR difference of opinion, as a result of which, the accused refused to marry her.
Under such circumstances, it cannot be said that the voluntary acts of the petitioner and respondent No.2 will give rise to invoking the penal provisions as alleged.
Hence, I am of the opinion that, registration of criminal case is in abuse of process of law.
Hence, the same is liable to be quashed.

Accordingly, I answer the above point in the 'affirmative'
and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The petition is allowed.

(ii) Criminal proceedings initiated against the petitioner in Crime No.16/2025 of Women Police Station, Vijayapura pending on the file of learned IV Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Vijayapura, for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n),
417, 504 of IPC is hereby quashed.
